Right page: a narrow strip at the right edge showing the start of the facing page's lines, which are marginal/outer text cut off by the scan edge; these are printed text of the facing page and are transcribed as notes on the right side.

main_text.p: antecedentes. Quare termini tres noti ad concludendumnund quartum sic disponentur:
Is quartus cum antecedentes omnes æquet, additus ul⁄timo 54, totus erit 8 0, progressionis summa.

Sit item hæc subsesquialtera: 16.24.36.54.81, reliqui secundi & ultimi termini sunt, 8 & 65. Unde ex tribus proportionalibus 8. 16. 65 concluditur quartus 130, qui ultimo excepto totus est ex antecedentibus: postremo igitur 81 adiectus, summam progressionis pandit 211. Unde apparet, cognito primo, secundo & ultimo progressionis terminis, summam quoque latere non posse.
main_text.head: Exemplum.

p.i: Quidam domum suam tritico persoluendam sic uendidit, ut ad primam ingressus ianuam granum unum, ad secundam duo, ad tertiam quatuor: atque ita secundum ianuarum numerum, dupla continue ratione progrediendo, soluëret. Qui a contractu recederet, alteri aureos 12 pœnæ loco penderet. Cum autem ianuæ domus 60 fuerint, nescitur tritici aceruus.

main_text.p: Tali conditione Basileæ aliquando uir admodum nummatus, cui Geometricæ progressionis mirum incrementum cognitum erat, domum suam inter pocula uesnuns

page.notes: Right edge strip shows cut-off words of the facing page: "nund", "uoca", "unui", "caper", "tur co", "Vn", "q"; these are fragments and are transcribed only where legible. The final word of the last line on the left page continues into the facing page at the gutter ("ues-" / "nuns") and is given as printed. Several numerals in the progression are uncertain in the scan, notably "81", "54" and "130".
